pages.text: $(l)Chimpanzees$() hold ground at the jungle's edge - fifty blocks round, and held hard. A stranger on it is warned with hooting and drumming; stay, and the patrol comes for you. The alpha will walk up and stand too close - hand it something, or hold $(k:hominin_evolution.think), within five seconds. Feed them, and a community that trusts you lets you pass, grooms you and mobs whatever chases you.

$(l)Bonobos$(), from erectus on, by rivers and forest edges. Nothing hunts within sixty-four blocks of a peaceful troop. They share food, groom you, and forage beside you.$(br2)Hurt one and that is over, for good, for every troop your people ever meet.
$(l)Dinopithecus$(), the giant baboon, never hunts you - but come within five blocks and it will not stop. A display does not work on it. Gone by erectus.

$(l)Paranthropus$() - the other hominin, until antecessor. They strip the ground for sixty blocks, so foraging near them comes up empty; drive them off with a display or a thrown stone.$(br2)They see cats first and shriek. They trade, sometimes badly, and will show you good stone or obsidian.
Baboons, chimpanzees and bonobos work the ground too: foraging within thirty-five blocks of them fails far more often than it should.

A baboon troop that trusts you comes $(l)begging$(). Hand one something within a minute and the troop grooms you and your band - and now and then leads you somewhere worth knowing. Ignore them and the trust goes: it has to be kept up with food.$(br2)Your band keeps well clear of the giant baboon now.

A chimpanzee community that trusts you comes out to meet you - two of them, well past the edge of their range - and walks with you while you are on their ground. The deeper into the jungle, the more communities, and the bigger.
